title: Operational signatures of exceptional quantum channels
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) are usually introduced as defective degeneracies of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and, in fully open quantum dynamics, of Liouvillian generators. Here we formulate an operational theory of exceptional points that does not invoke a Hamiltonian or a master equation. The primitive dynamical object is a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) quantum channel $Φ$, applied an integer number $n$ of times, while physical data are probabilities $p_n^{\mathbf A}(x|ρ)$ associated with states $ρ$ and observables $\mathbf A$ having measurements results $x$. We define exceptional channels through nontrivial Jordan chains of $Φ$ and show that a Jordan block of order $m$ generates discrete polynomial-exponential terms with maximal degree $m-1$. This places the physics of exceptional points in contact with what can be directly measured in experiments.
summary: This paper introduces an operational theory for exceptional points (EPs) by analyzing the repeated application of quantum channels ($\Phi^n$) rather than relying on Hamiltonians. It shows that the characteristic signature of an EP—a polynomial-exponential term—is not inherent to the dynamics but depends on the specific measurement observable used. This provides a direct, experimentally accessible diagnostic tool for identifying EPs in open quantum systems.
main_problem: To develop an operational theory for exceptional points (EPs) that bypasses the need for a Hamiltonian or a master equation.
main_result: The operational signature of an EP is revealed through discrete polynomial-exponential terms in the measurement probabilities, which depend critically on the specific measurement observable used.
method: The analysis uses the repeated application of a completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) quantum channel ($\Phi^n$) and relates the resulting probabilities to the Jordan chain structure of the channel superoperator.
model_or_system: The general system is described by a CPTP quantum channel ($\Phi$), which governs the evolution of the density matrix. A specific example uses a qubit model in a 2D Hilbert space analyzed via Pauli operators.
key_observables: The probability $p_A^n(x|ho) = 	ext{tr}[A(x)\Phi^n(ho)]$, particularly the transient term proportional to $n\lambda^{n-1}$.
important_parameters: The channel parameters ($	heta, \lambda$) defining the EP, and the measurement observable $A$ (or its corresponding measurement direction $\vec{m}$).
main_assumptions: The theory is formulated independently of PT symmetry, Lindblad equations, and continuous-time limits; the observable $A$ is assumed to be a POVM.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the dependence of the measured probability $p_+(n)$ on the measurement direction $\vec{m}$, showing the signature only for a specific direction $\vec{m}_a$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general operational framework using CPTP channels and Jordan chains. It then applies this framework to a concrete qubit model, explicitly calculating the time evolution and demonstrating the measurement dependence of the EP signature.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, measurement-centric framework to detect EPs in open quantum systems, moving the concept from purely Hamiltonian/Liouvillian analysis to directly measurable quantities.
